beats.say: Work phone lost or stolen? Do not feel embarrassed and do not wait. Every minute counts.
Call technical support at once from another phone. They can lock it remotely and check where it is.
A message like this may follow. It is an attempt to steal your password and unlock the phone.

messages.text: Your phone has been found. Sign in to see where it is:

beats.say: Even if the caller says they are technical support, never tell anyone your PIN or SMS code.

scenes.prompt: Your work phone is lost. Put the steps in order.

items.label: Call technical support from another phone
Have them lock the phone remotely
Call your operator and block the SIM
Change your work passwords from another device
If it is not found, have it wiped remotely

scenes.explain: Reporting and locking take minutes and stop most of the harm. Wiping comes last so the phone can still be found. If your organisation's procedure sets another order, follow it.

scenes.title: A call from support
scenes.intro: Your work phone went missing last night. This morning your personal number gets a call from technical support.

actions.label: Answer
actions.feedback: Answering is not dangerous. What matters is what you say.

actions.label: Decline
actions.feedback: That works too. Call technical support yourself on the official number.

steps.say: Hello, this is technical support. To lock your phone we sent you an SMS code. Please read it out.
steps.spoken: Hello, <breath> this is technical support. To lock your phone we sent you an SMS code. Please, uh, read it out.

actions.label: Read out the code
actions.feedback: That code is a sign-in to your account. Support does not need your code to lock a phone.

actions.label: I will call the official number myself
actions.feedback: Excellent. Checking on the official number exposes a fake call at once.

actions.label: Hang up
actions.feedback: Correct. Real technical support never asks for codes or passwords.

steps.say: All right, then tell me your screen lock PIN. We will unlock the phone remotely and save your data.
steps.spoken: All right, <sigh> then tell me your screen lock PIN. We will unlock the phone remotely and save your data.

actions.label: Tell the PIN
actions.feedback: Whoever has the phone will open it with this PIN. The management system never needs your PIN to lock it.

actions.label: I will not tell my PIN
actions.feedback: Correct. Your PIN is yours alone and is never shared.

actions.label: Hang up
actions.feedback: Good decision. When the pressure rises, ending the call is the right move.

steps.label: The call has ended. What now?

actions.label: Call technical support's official number
actions.feedback: Correct. Report this call, because the attacker knows your name and number.

actions.label: Do nothing
actions.feedback: The attacker will call another colleague next. If you report it, support can warn everyone.

scenes.prompt: Messages after the phone was lost. Safe, or a threat?

messages.text: Your phone has been found. Sign in to see it on the map:

cards.explain: A fake found message is after your password. Only technical support checks where the phone is.

messages.text: Your SIM card has been blocked at your request. Bring your ID card to a sales office for a new one.

cards.explain: No link, nothing is requested, and it confirms your own request. This is a normal notice.

body.text: Your work phone has been locked remotely. Come to the 2nd floor tomorrow at 10:00 for a new device.

cards.explain: The address is your organisation's, with no link and no password request. This answers your report.

body.text: I have your phone. Transfer 100 AZN and I will give it back. Tell the police and I will leak what is on it.

cards.explain: Do not send money and keep the conversation. Show it to technical support and the police.

nodes.text: At home in the evening you realise you left your work phone in a taxi. It is 22:00.

choices.label: I call technical support right now
choices.feedback: Correct. You can report at night too, and the phone is locked at once.

choices.label: I wait until morning, maybe the driver will call
choices.feedback: A lot can be done with a phone in one night. Report now, and if the driver calls, even better.

nodes.text: Hello, you left your phone in my taxi last night. I brought it in, it was locked, I touched nothing.
nodes.speaker: Taxi driver (in the morning, at the office)
nodes.spoken: Hello, you left your phone in my taxi last night. <breath> I brought it in, it was locked, I touched nothing.

choices.label: I hand it to technical support to check
choices.feedback: Excellent. A phone that was out of your hands needs checking, and the specialist decides.

choices.label: I unlock it and get straight back to work
choices.feedback: The phone spent a night in someone else's hands. Let technical support check it first.

question.prompt: What protects your data best when a phone is lost?

options.label: A PIN of at least 6 digits plus fingerprint
options.feedback: Correct. A long PIN is hard to guess, and a fingerprint keeps daily use easy.

options.label: A 4-digit PIN with your birth year
options.feedback: A birth year is easy to find on social media. Pick at least 6 random digits.

options.label: A simple unlock pattern
options.feedback: A simple pattern can be read from smudges on the screen or over your shoulder.

options.label: No lock, the phone is always with me
options.feedback: A phone can be lost in a moment. Without a lock, work mail is open to anyone.

scenes.explain: A strong screen lock is the first barrier protecting data on a lost phone.

points: If the phone is lost, call technical support at once from another phone.
Never tell anyone a code, PIN or password, whoever is calling.
Have a returned phone checked by technical support before you use it.
